knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$, where $R$ is the union of the following rectangles and

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}3 y&1<x<3,\ 0<y<1\\x^{2} y&1<x<3,\ 1<y<3.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}R_1&=(1,3)\times(0,1)\\R_2&=(1,3)\times(1,3)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Apply additivity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\sum_{j=1}^{2} I_j,\\I_j&=\iint_{R_j}f\,\mathrm{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_1$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_1}(3 y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{3}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{0}^{1}(3 y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{1}^{3}\left[\frac{3 y^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}\\&=\left(\left(3\right)-(\left(1\right))\right)\left(\frac{3 \left(1\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{3 \left(0\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(2\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=3\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_2$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_2}(x^{2} y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{3}(x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{3}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{1}^{3}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{3}\\&=\left(\frac{\left(3\right)^{3}}{3}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{3}}{3}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\left(3\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(\frac{26}{3}\right)\left(4\right)=\frac{104}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(3\right)\\&\quad+\left(\frac{104}{3}\right)\\&=\boxed{\frac{113}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$, where $R$ is the union of the following rectangles and

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}\frac{x}{y}&-1<x<0,\ 1<y<3\\- 2 y&0<x<1,\ 1<y<3.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}R_1&=(-1,0)\times(1,3)\\R_2&=(0,1)\times(1,3)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Apply additivity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\sum_{j=1}^{2} I_j,\\I_j&=\iint_{R_j}f\,\mathrm{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_1$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_1}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{-1}^{0}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{-1}^{0}\left[\ln{\left(y \right)}\right]_{1}^{3}\\&=\left(\frac{\left(0\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(-1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\left(\ln{\left(\left(3\right) \right)}-(\ln{\left(\left(1\right) \right)})\right)\\&=\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\ln{\left(3 \right)}\right)=- \frac{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_2$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_2}(- 2 y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{0}^{1}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{3}(- 2 y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{0}^{1}\left[- y^{2}\right]_{1}^{3}\\&=\left(\left(1\right)-(\left(0\right))\right)\left(- \left(3\right)^{2}-(- \left(1\right)^{2})\right)\\&=\left(1\right)\left(-8\right)=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(- \frac{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2}\right)\\&\quad+\left(-8\right)\\&=\boxed{-8 - \frac{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions
error_recipes: omit x primitive denominator in region 1
omit y primitive denominator in region 2

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$, where $R$ is the union of the following rectangles and

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}3&1<x<4,\ 1<y<4\\\frac{1}{4 \sqrt{x} \sqrt{y}}&4<x<9,\ 1<y<4.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}R_1&=(1,4)\times(1,4)\\R_2&=(4,9)\times(1,4)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Apply additivity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\sum_{j=1}^{2} I_j,\\I_j&=\iint_{R_j}f\,\mathrm{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_1$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_1}(3)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{4}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{4}(3)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{1}^{4}\left[3 y\right]_{1}^{4}\\&=\left(\left(4\right)-(\left(1\right))\right)\left(3 \left(4\right)-(3 \left(1\right))\right)\\&=\left(3\right)\left(9\right)=27\end{aligned}
$$

On $R_2$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{R_2}\left(\frac{1}{4 \sqrt{x} \sqrt{y}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{4}^{9}\left(\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{4}\left(\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\sqrt{x}\right]_{4}^{9}\left[\sqrt{y}\right]_{1}^{4}\\&=\left(\sqrt{\left(9\right)}-(\sqrt{\left(4\right)})\right)\left(\sqrt{\left(4\right)}-(\sqrt{\left(1\right)})\right)\\&=\left(1\right)\left(1\right)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(27\right)\\&\quad+\left(1\right)\\&=\boxed{28}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions
error_recipes: add x endpoint values in region 1
add y endpoint values in region 2
